title: Herbert Hall's career and move to Texas
summary: Herbert Hall went on with Eddie Condon, married in Texas, and is settling there; he came from a family of nine musicians.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I think I found it somewhere. I know Herbert Hall has gone on with Eddie Condon.

Yeah, he's getting ready to settle in Texas. He's going to come south again? That's right. They bought his wife. We introduced his wife to him when we first came to San Antonio, Texas. And he married her right around 20, around 29 or 30. And her parents are from a little town of Bernie, and they had a lot of land up there. And they willed it to his wife. Mm-hmm. So Herbert visited me sometime this year. Mm-hmm. And they built a fabulous home up there, and he's leaving New York altogether. Well, I can understand that.
Yeah. Yeah. Jimmy Condon just died, and that's the guy that he played with most of the year. Mm-hmm.
Sure, he had his rough moments up there. Yes, he did.

New York was not easy. But fortunately he fell into his brother's footsteps. See, Edmund's name was big. Mm-hmm. So there wasn't any problem, because Herbert can play. Oh, I agree with you that. So there wasn't any problem for him to pick up in his brother's footsteps.
I'm trying to think of who I've ever heard of him playing with in the way of big bands other than yours.
Yeah. None. He played around... He's confined to small bands. He played around in Baton Rouge some, I think he told me. Of course, was there, or whatever.

Oh, well, that's where he's from. Yeah. But not after he left my band. Yeah, I guess so. He's going back to before he came to my band and Reserva and up in there. There was nine brothers, all of them were musicians. Yeah. Including the daddy.
